rulings.title: claim-gate bypass (withdraw-to-zero then autoAnnihilate)

analysis.assetRisk: NONE, and this survives independently of the owner's disclaimer. Conservation is measured exact: INV-1/INV-2 PASS with max observed overshoot over the emission ceiling = 0 across 640,640 Foundry + 302,817 Medusa calls, and the 1024-wei DUST_SLACK was never consumed. I checked the phUSD-backing leg separately, because the V2 'Antimatter is redeemable into unbacked phUSD' premise is exactly where a hidden dilution would live: it is not there. Antimatter.annihilate is permissionless and consumes the CALLER'S OWN stable half, so a raw-minted backlog sitting in a staker's wallet can only become phUSD if that staker supplies the stable themselves. The bypass therefore changes WHO sources the stable half (the staker's returned principal instead of their booked principal) and WHEN, not whether the resulting phUSD is backed. No incremental Antimatter, no unbacked phUSD, no dilution of other stakers, no protocol funds moved (INV-3 PASS).
analysis.attackPath: Valid, concrete, cheap and permissionless. Verified in source: withdraw books the whole pending reward at :415-419 with no gate; autoAnnihilate(token, 0) collapses capped to 0 so excessBase is the entire backlog, minted raw at :605. Fuzzer-shrunk to 1 call (INV-5 FAIL) and replayed deterministically for 100% of entitlement. The path being real is NOT in dispute here; only its consequence is.
analysis.conditions: None. Works with the gate shut, needs no capital, no MEV, no race, and works while the FOREIGN Antimatter contract is paused (antimatter.mint is not whenNotPaused) when the ordinary annihilate path is dead.
analysis.impact: The DELIVERY FORM and TIMING of the staker's own entitlement. Availability is increased, not impaired. No third party bears a cost.

rulings.whyNotMedium: Each Medium limb is independently unreached. (i) Assets at risk: none, per measured conservation and the backing analysis above. (ii) Protocol function/availability impacted: the C4 limb is about a function being IMPAIRED, not about a UX throttle being more permissive than documented; the party receiving the value is the party entitled to it. (iii) Value leak with stated assumptions: nothing leaves the system and no counterparty is short. A defeated pedagogical throttle whose entire effect is to change when an entitled party receives their own accrued balance is squarely the QA/Low 'function incorrect as to spec' limb.

n24_4cRuling.question: Is the classifier's 'the owner disclaims reliance, therefore there is nothing to break' argument sound, or is it 4(c) evasion by another name?
n24_4cRuling.verdict: THE DISTINCTION IS SOUND, but it is not the leg the Low should rest on, and this audit re-grounds it.
n24_4cRuling.reasoning: 4(c) is a one-directional rule: it forbids using the CLOSED state of the gate as a mitigation that lowers some OTHER finding's impact. The classifier makes no such move — it never says 'this matters less because the gate is shut'. Its move is the opposite: the gate is the very thing bypassed, and the note establishes what the gate IS (a UX mechanism, not an access control). Section 4's own preamble concedes that in-source prose 'can only establish intent', and what kind of control claimEnabled is, is precisely an intent question and a legitimate input to whether defeating it impairs protocol function. So the argument is formally distinct from a 4(c) discount and is admissible.
n24_4cRuling.residualTension: There is real tension worth stating plainly. 4(a) permits the note to suppress exactly ONE thing (the Law-2 'accidental bypass' framing), and 4(b) declares this precise mechanism a live Law-1 lead the note may NOT suppress. Leaning on the note's closing paragraph to zero the IMPACT of the finding 4(b) protects comes close to reaching the same result by a different door. It does not cross the line here for two reasons: the classifier does not suppress the finding (it reports it at Low, loudly, with the falsified rationale intact and routed to spec-conformance as F-01), and the Low stands up with the disclaimer struck entirely — strike CLAUDE.md:184-203 from the record and INV-1/INV-2's zero-overshoot plus the phUSD-backing analysis still leave no Medium limb reached. That is the test I applied, and it passes.
n24_4cRuling.instruction: Re-order the justification so the measured-conservation and backing legs carry the rating and the owner's disclaimer appears only as corroboration. As written, the disclaimer reads as load-bearing, which is what invites the 4(c) objection.

rulings.understatementCheck: Actively looked for and not found. The three escalation candidates were each run down: (a) the THIRD ungated mint path at _exitPosition:845-850 found by spec-conformance — real, but the source itself declares it 'DELIBERATELY UNGATED ... migration is never brickable', so it adds a third Law-2 falsification to F-01 and zero severity; (b) working during a foreign Antimatter pause — a genuine asymmetry (informed stakers get paid, uninformed ones are locked out) and correctly carried on CLASS-001, but it is an argument against calling the bypass an acceptable escape valve, not an asset-risk limb; (c) premature raw Antimatter entering circulation under the void minter-cushion suppression — refuted by the backing analysis above.
rulings.mustNotBeLost: The FALSIFIED RATIONALE is the reportable core and the classifier is right that it RAISES rather than lowers the weight of this Low. N24 bullet 2 reasons only about organic accrual growing the numerator and never about a caller shrinking the denominator in one transaction; story-025's 'becomes the only reward path' is false three ways over. The owner will size the teaching phase against a bound that does not exist. A reader who takes 'Low' as 'skippable' has misread this entry.
rulings.notes: Concur with flaggedForHumanReview: true. This is the correct call and it is also the run's most consequential Low.

rulings.title: reward-forfeiture trap (underwater + short buffer -> emergencyWithdraw destroys the backlog)

analysis.assetRisk: Real and irreversible. 4166666666666666550000 wei of Antimatter entitlement destroyed at :633 (unclaimedReward zeroed, nothing minted), reproduced deterministically with three controls. Under the V2 premise the minter-cushion and opportunity-cost suppressions are VOID, so this is user value and not marketing spend. Principal is untouched.
analysis.attackPath: No attacker. Verified in source, all four legs: claim reverts on claimEnabled (:440, default false at :100), withdraw reverts via _routeExit guardUnderwater=true (:423 -> :1184-1194), autoAnnihilate reverts on the same guard (:579), emergencyWithdraw is the sole survivor and forfeits (:633).
analysis.conditions: SEE THE CORRECTION BELOW. The finding's stated two-part conjunction is wrong; the real gate is one condition.
analysis.impact: 100% of the accrued reward backlog destroyed on the only path that returns principal.

requiredCorrection.severity: MUST FIX before submission — this is an UNDERSTATEMENT inside a Medium, i.e. a finding about the finding
requiredCorrection.whatIsWrong: classified.json states likelihood 'MEDIUM, and honestly conditional -- it requires the conjunction of an underwater strategy AND a buffer short of the request ... but the conjunction is a real gate and this classification does not assume the worst case', and describes condition (ii) as 'the EXPECTED state at scale'.
requiredCorrection.whyItIsWrong: I verified this against source rather than against the finding text. _routeDeposit (:1139-1144) forwards 100% of every deposit to the wired strategy and retains nothing; stake (:388-389) and depositFor (:941) both credit only what the strategy returns. Nothing in src/ ever funds an idle balance: setYieldStrategy sweeps idle balance INTO the strategy (:349-354), relinquishPrincipal moves no assets, and no donate/target-buffer/reserve mechanism exists in the contract at all (donateBuffer is a test-harness function, not production code). The idle buffer is therefore ZERO on a freshly deployed pool and stays zero unless somebody transfers tokens in unprompted. The PoC log confirms it empirically: 'idle buffer held by StableStakerV2: 0'. Condition (ii) is not a conjunct that gates reachability at scale — it is the DEPLOYMENT DEFAULT. Reachability collapses to the single condition 'the wired strategy is below par', which the owner's own triage of 69c7666eee describes as the normal case the buffer exists for.
requiredCorrection.replacementText: likelihood: HIGH for the TRAP STATE. Condition (ii) (idle buffer < the request) is the deployment default, not a conjunct: nothing in StableStakerV2 funds an idle balance, so a fresh pool holds zero and _routeExit's underwater branch reverts for every caller. The trap state is entered by the single external condition 'strategy below par'. The loss itself remains elective: it lands only when a staker chooses emergencyWithdraw rather than waiting.
consequentialEdits: classification.attackPath step 2 - strike 'this is the EXPECTED state at scale, not an edge case' and state that it is the default state from block one.

justification - the sentence 'the conjunction is a real gate and this classification does not assume the worst case' is factually false and must go. The correct statement is that the CONSEQUENCE is gated (by the staker's election), not the STATE.

flagReason - 'If the owner judges the underwater + buffer-short conjunction to be operationally unreachable at the deployed buffer sizing' invites a triage decision on a premise that does not hold, because there is no buffer sizing to reach. Re-word so the owner is asked the right question: how long can a wired strategy sit below par with claimEnabled false?

pocStatus - stale. It says a standalone deterministic PoC is OWED; reports/stable-staker/17/poc/Run17_M01_RewardForfeitureTrap.out.txt shows 5/5 passing including three controls (gate-open defusal, pre-story-025 ungated claim, funded buffer). Mark it DELIVERED.

rulings.whyNotHigh: I tested the upgrade seriously and it does not carry, on one dispositive discriminator. C4 High requires that assets CAN be stolen/lost via the attack path itself; here the path produces a STATE in which every exit but one is shut, and the loss materialises only when the staker elects the one exit whose single documented rule is 'no reward, principal out' (N4 rules that forfeiture intentional). The validator's own probe is decisive and points AGAINST escalation: an untouched backlog keeps accruing (4.166e21 -> 1.825e22 wei over a simulated year), so nothing is destroyed on a timer and a staker who does not need their principal loses nothing by waiting. That is a coerced choice under duress, not a loss inflicted by the protocol - the classic Medium shape of 'availability impacted plus value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'. No attacker, no theft, no third-party gain, principal intact, and the strategy's underwater condition is externally driven. Default-state reachability raises the LIKELIHOOD of the trap state, and it moves this to the top of the Medium band, but it does not convert an elective loss into a direct one.
rulings.whyNotLow: Never in play. Real irreversible destruction of redeemable value, in a state reached by ordinary market movement with no adversary, newly created by this diff range (before story-025 claim() was ungated, so a trapped staker could claim then hatch out). The 'the owner can just open the gate, so it is Low' move is exactly what N24 4(c) forbids and it was correctly not taken.
rulings.n24_4cRuling: COMPLIANT on the load-bearing question. One caution: the classifier cites 'one owner transaction defuses it entirely' as a reason it is not High. That is remedy-availability, not the 4(c)-forbidden closed-state discount, so it is admissible - but it is the WEAKEST leg of the Medium and must not carry weight alone, precisely because the finding's own footgun is that the operational obligation is UNWRITTEN for the underwater trigger (CLAUDE.md writes it down only for the rarer antimatter-pause trigger, N23). A remedy nobody is told to apply is not a reliable cap. Let the elective-loss discriminator carry the not-High call; demote the one-transaction argument to corroboration.

crossCuttingObservation.raisedBy: this audit, not present in classified.json
crossCuttingObservation.statement: The 'shared idle buffer' that N19, 69c7666eee's wont-fix triage ('sized for daily-volume withdrawals'), CLASS-004 and CLASS-006 all reason about HAS NO FUNDING MECHANISM IN THE CONTRACT. It is not sized, tuned or replenished by any code path; it is whatever tokens happen to be sitting in StableStakerV2. Every argument in this run and in the ledger that treats buffer adequacy as a configurable operational parameter rests on a premise the source does not support.
crossCuttingObservation.consequence: While a strategy is below par, withdraw is dead for EVERY staker and not merely the trapped one, so the availability limb of CLASS-004 is broader than the finding states. It also bears directly on the owner's quoted sizing input in 69c7666eee.
crossCuttingObservation.action: Route to human triage alongside CLASS-006's addendum on 69c7666eee. Do NOT mint a new fingerprint from this audit; it is an input to the owner's re-check, not an independent finding.

rulings.notes: Medium CONFIRMED, at the top of the band. Concur with flaggedForHumanReview: true. If the owner's triage answer to the corrected question is that a strategy may sit below par for a sustained period with the gate shut, this entry should be re-weighed and I would not stand in the way of a High at that point.

rulings.title: exit-shortfall floor blind to a fee-charging ERC4626 vault
rulings.justification: This is the textbook right answer to a refuted-but-not-dead finding and I would not change a word of the disposition. The Medium availability limb was killed by measurement performed THIS run against live mainnet state (block 25878600, cold-cache re-fetched, autoDOLA 0.473 bps / autoUSD 0.535 bps against a 1.00 bp allowance) with Halmos corroborating the boundary exactly and check_control_5bp failing as a positive control - so the harness demonstrably can find the brick when one exists, which is what makes this a real negative rather than an untested one. Filing it as a live Medium would be precisely the overstatement the pipeline rejects. Equally, closing it would be the Law-1 error: the trigger is an external Tokemak governance parameter, the margin is half a basis point, the deciding constants are `constant` with no setter so there is no operator response, and nothing in the runbook ties reward-path liveness to a foreign vault's fee. Retaining it at Low with an armed, monitorable trigger and an explicit doNotClose is the correct handling of an externally-triggered availability risk. The interaction with CLASS-013 is well caught and should stay in the report: a config record naming a non-ERC4626 contract as autoDOLA means the reassuring 0.473 bps measurement describes the CORRECT autopool, not necessarily the one the config would deploy against.

rulings.title: dust-window liveness failure (1 wei owed -> 'exit shortfall')
rulings.justification: Low is right and the 50/17,729 (0.28%) observation does not move it. Two things cap this and both hold. It is SELF-HEALING - the owed dust stays in unclaimedReward and the call succeeds once further accrual crosses the boundary, so no value is destroyed and no path is permanently closed; and the amount in the trigger window is by construction sub-share-price dust. Neither the asset limb nor the availability limb is reached by a transient revert on a dust-sized request. I checked the evidence quality specifically, because a 0.28% observed rate is the kind of number that tempts inflation: it holds up - 46 of the 50 hits landed on pool 1, the REAL ERC4626YieldStrategy over a real OZ vault, and the fixtureCaveats correctly disqualify only the FEE conclusions while leaving the ROUNDING conclusions load-bearing. The scaling law is honestly caged as demonstrated at an unrealistic 1247 assets/share and explicitly not a live finding at stablecoin-autopool prices, which is the right restraint. The real cost is diagnostic and is correctly stated: the revert accuses an honest strategy of lying. Keeping it separate from CLASS-002 is correct - opposite ends of the size axis, opposite evidence status, different remedies. Endorse the warning that EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE must be neither raised for this nor lowered.

rulings.title: zero-principal backlog holder has no reward path on a Migrating pool
rulings.justification: I am holding this at Low but I am not comfortable leaving it as an ordinary Low, and the classifier half-saw why: its own n24_4c_compliance note concedes 'this is the one place the rating brushes against 4(c)'. The concession understates it. The user is locked out of value they own, they have NO self-remedy (claim is gated at :440, autoAnnihilate requires Active at :517, userMigrate requires amount > 0 at :866, emergencyWithdraw requires Active and forfeits at :625/:633 - I verified all four), and BOTH escape routes offered are owner-only: setClaimEnabled(true), or reviving the pool to Active. The classifier's argument that 'reopening the gate is a convenience, not the only remedy' does not do the work it is asked to do, because the alternative is equally owner-gated. The reason this user is stuck IS the closed gate, and 'the value survives so it is Low' is close to the shape 4(c) exists to prevent. What holds the Low, and it does hold, is that no value is DESTROYED and the C4 Medium availability limb is about the protocol's function, not one user class's convenience pending an owner action expected anyway - plus the state needs a genuine conjunction (fully-withdrawn-but-unclaimed AND an owner-initiated terminal migration).
rulings.requiredHandling: Do not leave this as a plain Low. Give it the SAME treatment CLASS-002 received, which is the run's own correct template for a conditional finding: arm an explicit escalation trigger - 'escalate to Medium if a terminal migration is initiated on any pool while claimEnabled is false' - and record the 4(c) tension on the entry so a human triages it rather than inheriting it. Under the symmetry rule a borderline call must not be silently resolved downward; this one is resolved downward with the reasoning visible and an armed trigger, which is the acceptable form.
rulings.alsoCorrect: The expiredClosure handling of f1661ec524 is exactly right - rationale aged out because sibling code changed, its own bucket, not a regression, not an incomplete fix, no patch to restore, no auto-flip. That is the distinction this project has got wrong before and it is got right here.

rulings.title: autoAnnihilate draws tolerance-inflated GROSS from the shared buffer (rate disclosure)
rulings.justification: Low and the ADDENDUM disposition are both right, and the disclosure discipline is exemplary - filing on autoAnnihilate mints a different fingerprint for a root cause already fingerprinted on _routeExit, and with 28/46 fingerprint drift on this project dedup would have waved it through as new, so naming 69c7666eee and 2b9a89d29c explicitly and quoting the triage verbatim is precisely what is required rather than a silent re-file. On the merits Low is correct: no NEW exposure (gross is capped at the caller's own principal at :558, and the caller is value-neutral against their own books), NIL on the current wiring where previewExitFor is the capped identity so surplus is always 0 and the :607-609 leg is dead code, and latent only against a future market strategy. The one new element is honestly narrow and honestly stated - the RATE, 1/(1-slip) times more buffer per unit of reward than the transaction needs, against an owner sizing input quoted as 'daily-volume withdrawals'. The refusals of N19 (cited authority does not exist in CLAUDE.md at HEAD) and N20 (covers an extraction framing this finding does not make) are both correct. SA-17-01 above sharpens this entry rather than changing its severity: there is no buffer sizing to re-check because nothing funds the buffer, which makes the rate observation more pointed, not less.

rulings.title: cross-repo route: StableStakerV2:556 is previewExitFor's first production consumer
rulings.justification: Correctly handled as a ledger-reconciliation obligation with severityBearing: false, so it is neither dropped nor allowed to inflate the finding count - a defect it is not. The substance is right and its nuance should be carried rather than flattened: reflax WATCH-17-03's premise ('previewExitFor has ZERO CONSUMERS across all nine top-level submodule HEADs') is now demonstrably false, L-18 and L-23 arm while L-22 does not (preview at :556 and execution at :579 sit in the same transaction with no intervening external call, nonReentrant, CEI intact - I checked), and L-19's fee leg is partly settled by this run's fork measurement. The critical caveat is the load-bearing part and must survive into the report: L-18's dominance rests on TWO invariants no test pins, so the DominanceRun17Grounding test is doing real work. Note that L-23's Low rating EXPIRES on V2 deployment, which pairs with the preDeployment framing - this is the right moment to reconcile, not after.

rulings.title: CLAUDE.md headline states the superseded NET debit
rulings.justification: Low -> QA is the correct downgrade and one of the few places in this run where something was moved DOWN. Nothing behavioural turns on it: the code is correct (autoAnnihilate debits the GROSS at :565-566) and a later bullet in the same section states the correct semantics, so the document contradicts itself rather than misdescribing the code outright. The two reasons it is kept visible rather than dropped are both good ones and are worth more than its severity: the defect sits in the DECLARED KNOWN-ISSUES SOURCE, which lowers confidence in every suppression extracted from that section and should be carried into the next run's extraction note; and it is the second CLAUDE.md-documents-a-superseded-model entry on this project after ss9f3-clau. Routing to spec-conformance as F-03 rather than burying it in the QA bundle is correct under Law 2.

rulings.title: autoAnnihilateAvailable returns true where autoAnnihilate reverts; probe near-vacuous
rulings.justification: Low is right and is independently capped by the standing C4 rule that view-function issues are QA/Low at best; Low rather than QA because the view is CONSUMED by the UI it was written for, not unused - that is the correct side of the line. Impact is a misleading UI and gas wasted on a reverting transaction, no asset or availability limb. The vacuity analysis is unusually good and I re-derived it: the principalOf != 0 early-return at :1058 already guarantees clientBalances >= 1, so for the direct strategy the 1-unit probe at :1061 is a tautology, and for the market strategy ceilDiv(1*MAX_BPS, MAX_BPS - slip) == 1 for any slip < 5000 bps - the view detects exactly one condition, a 100% slippage tolerance. The refusal of N26 is correct: N26 governs the preview INSIDE autoAnnihilate being untrusted and re-measured, which says nothing about a PUBLIC view's contract with its callers, and neither N26 nor N18 reaches the principalOf == 0 early-return. Keeping this split from CLASS-001 is right - same line, two impacts, two fixes.

rulings.title: docs describe only the un-grossed underwater draw; no test covers autoAnnihilate underwater
rulings.justification: Held at Low rather than dropped to QA on the correct ground: the falsified claim is BEHAVIOURAL, not editorial. CLAUDE.md's round-3 carve-out says _routeExit 'returns the nominal amount without measuring anything' and story-025's checklist says the idle buffer is 'UNTOUCHED across every case', and both are false at HEAD - surplus is transferred out of the shared buffer at :609 and relinquishPrincipal(token, gross) writes booked principal down by the inflated figure. The test-gap half is the sharper finding of the two: round 3 corrected MockYieldStrategy.previewExitFor SPECIFICALLY so the underwater case could be tested, the correction landed and the test did not, and that absent test is the one that would have surfaced CLASS-006. Keeping it separate from CLASS-006 is right - different remedies (doc edit plus test, versus an owner sizing re-check) and different audiences. N19 correctly refused suppression, on the same ground as elsewhere in the run: its cited authority section does not exist in the file, and it cannot suppress a finding whose entire content is that this documentation is wrong.

rulings.title: the stated bound on the raw-mint path is the slippage tolerance; the real bound includes clientBalances
rulings.justification: Correctly held at Low in BOTH directions and the reasoning for each refusal is sound. Not raised: conservation is verified (INV-1/INV-2, zero overshoot) and the second cap is PROTOCOL-level, not caller-steerable - both previewExitFor implementations cap grossToRequest at clientBalances, and on ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy it binds structurally because _acquireShares books the haircut creditedPrincipal, so there is no vector for a caller to aim it. The explicit refusal to reach for the value-leak limb is the right restraint. Not dropped to QA: what is falsified is a SECURITY BOUND the owner reasons from in the story's own front-running analysis, not prose. The N20 refusal deserves to be quoted in the report as written - N20 is not a neighbour that happens to overlap, it IS the claim this finding falsifies, and a known issue cannot suppress the finding demonstrating that the known issue's own reasoning is incomplete. Keeping it strictly distinct from CLASS-001 (stated bound versus existence of a wider channel; doc edit versus design question) is correct, and the story-faithfulness agent reaching the same split independently is meaningful corroboration.

rulings.title: carryover: addresses.json records autoDOLA as a Vesper vault
rulings.justification: Low is right because the failure is FAIL-LOUD at an attended moment: asset() and totalAssets() revert on the recorded address, so deploying against this record produces a hard construction failure rather than a silent runtime defect, and no asset or availability limb is reached in a deployed system. The C4 third-party-dependency exclusion correctly does not apply - the defect is a wrong on-chain address RECORD, not a bug in someone else's contract. The ledger handling is right too (record under crossRepoRoutes, carry the re-confirmation date onto reflax 0c12a2cfaf, do not mint a stable-staker fingerprint). The reason it earns its place in a stable-staker run is well argued and should stay: CLASS-002's entire liveness argument turns on which autopool is wired.

overstatementScan.detail: No finding in this run claims more than its evidence carries. I specifically probed the places where inflation usually hides: CLASS-004's Medium is backed by a passing PoC with three controls rather than by narrative; CLASS-002's Medium case was actively REFUTED by this run's own measurement and the finding was held down rather than carried at its arrival severity; CLASS-003's 0.28% observed rate was not inflated into an availability claim and its scaling law is honestly caged as non-live; CLASS-012 explicitly declines the value-leak limb; CLASS-009 was moved DOWN to QA; and CLASS-007 was given severityBearing: false so a process obligation cannot pad the count. The run also correctly declines to describe CLASS-001 as over-minting, dilution or theft.
